items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: And he would pull up Bob Crosby's band bus.

ctx.x: Yeah. Always. In fact, it's, I've always remarked that among the organized black bands, there was always great deal of pride in playing. And they were respected. And they almost always made an extreme effort to look the part. Always. I can say that of any of the black bands that I ever saw. I'm, I'm barring country blues players and others who. You mean the big bands, you're talking about the name bands. I'm speaking of territorial bands, organized black bands. They were very good. And they, that's the only thing…

And Tom told me, Don Albert once told me that he'd be out on the road. And times would be hard. And I would be eating cheese and crackers. And he would pull up Bob Crosby's band bus. And they'd just need it. And all, that was the way you lived. You ate cheese and crackers and shared, shared alike. That's an unbelievable period.
Well, I can tell you, and I may be repeating myself for my former interview, but, uh, Jasper Tompkins, who was our agent.
